ideas.title: A bottom-bar quick-info widget, with one door anything can speak through
ideas.description:
Antonio, 2026-09-08, after seeing the refused-pick message land in the status bar: the bar should be a proper widget for short-lived information, styled, with a central API so a plugin or any component can put a line there.

WHAT EXISTS TODAY, AND WHY IT IS NOT THIS
`AppState.status_note: Option<String>` — added with P082(F003)/T475. A pick with nothing to offer writes one sentence there, `chrome_status` (heca/src/chrome/theme.rs) appends it to the status text, and the next keypress clears it (heca/src/app/input.rs, at the top of `handle_keyboard_input`). It works and it is deliberately plain, but it is:

- **a string on `AppState`, not a widget.** The whole bar is one `Label` built from `format!("{pane_count} panes | {focus_title} | {mode_str}{tail}")`. There is no styling to give a message, no icon, no severity, no room for two things at once, and no way to draw the message differently from the pane count beside it.
- **host-private.** `state.status_note = Some(..)` is reachable only from inside the app. A plugin has no way to say anything there, and neither does a component that is not holding `&mut AppState`. That is the ⭐⭐ RULE ZERO failure: there is no line a plugin author could write.
- **one message, last writer wins.** Two things with something to say silently overwrite each other.

The toast stack was tried first and rejected by Antonio for this case: a key that could not do its thing is not an event worth covering the work with an overlay. So the two are not substitutes — a notification is an *event*, this is a *reply to what you just did*, and they want different surfaces. Whatever is built here must not become a second notification system; see the note on ownership below.

WHAT TO BUILD (to be designed, not decided here)
- A **widget** in `heca-grid-ui` for the bar's transient region: domain-neutral, theme-driven, able to show a short line with a severity and optionally an icon, and to fold to nothing when there is nothing to say (`Visibility` already does the folding — see the rule on its entry in docs/widgets.md).
- **One door to speak through**, reachable from all three surfaces AGENTS requires: the app, a plugin, and RPC. The test is the one in RULE ZERO — write the line a plugin author would type. If it needs a registry, an id, or a host-private type, the API is missing.
- **A lifetime rule stated once.** Today's is "until the next keypress", which suits a reply to a key. A message from a background job wants something else — a duration, or until it is replaced. Whatever the answer, it belongs to the widget or the door, never to each caller: a rule every caller has to remember is the bug.
- **What happens when two things speak at once** — a queue, a priority, or a refusal. Today the second silently wins.

QUESTIONS TO SETTLE BEFORE BUILDING
- Is this the notification system's presentation for a `Toast`-unworthy severity, or a separate channel? Two systems that both put text on screen is exactly the "second path" AGENTS forbids — but a status reply and a notification genuinely differ in lifetime and in who dismisses them. Decide it explicitly rather than by which one gets built first.
- Does the bar keep its current fixed content (pane count | focus | mode) as segments, the way `[appearance.pane] title_segments` already configures the pane info bar? If so this is a segment kind, not a bolt-on, and the whole bar becomes configurable in the same breath.
- Who owns the bar's layout — is it a `ChromeRegion` with children, so a plugin could contribute a segment as well as a message?

WHERE THE CURRENT CODE IS
heca/src/chrome/theme.rs `chrome_status`; heca/src/app/render.rs `status_mode_parts`; heca/src/app_state.rs `status_note`; heca/src/app/input.rs (the clear); heca/src/handlers.rs `pick_refusal` (its first and only caller).

Once the door exists, `pick_refusal` should speak through it like anything else, and `status_note` should go.
